newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian man guilty of petrol attack on boy.
newsitem.headline: Australian man guilty of petrol attack on boy.

text.p: An Australian charity worker was found guilty on Wednesday of the attempted murder of a six-year-old boy he doused with petrol and set alight.

Paul Wade Streeton, 27, had pleaded innocent to attempted murder after he doused Aboriginal schoolboy Tjandamurra O'Shane with petrol and set him alight in a schoolyard in Cairns in the north of Queensland state last October.
Streeton, who pleaded guilty to causing grievous bodily harm, will be sentenced on Thursday.

In an audio tape played to the Cairns Supreme Court during the two-day trial, Streeton told police he had chosen O'Shane at random as "a sort of payback" for mistreatment he said he had received as a child.

The court heard that Streeton told police he had been planning the attack "on and off" since he was in primary school. As a child, he said, he was treated as if he was mentally retarded by his family, teachers, friends and neighbours.
The court heard Streeton had told police he wanted the death penalty and was not interested in "being incarcerated or rehabilitated". Capital punishment is not used in Australia.
Streeton turned himself in to police shortly after the attack. He had been reported missing by former colleagues at a charity collection agency from which he resigned a few days before the attack.

O'Shane received burns to 60 percent of his body when he was set alight in front of his primary school classmates. Now seven, he was in hospital for more than three months and had numerous skin graft operations.
O'Shane is the nephew of a prominent Aboriginal magistrate.
